title: Degree-one character lift extension and adjunction normalization
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring and $G$ a profinite group, with internal equivariant modules, the homogeneous resolution $P$ and augmentation $e:P\to A[0]$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution, lem-sfb-internal-bar-roof-adjunction]. Let $a:\underline G\to(A,+)$ be an additive condensed character, with extension boundary $\delta_a$ and positive class $[a]$ of [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class]. For every quasi-isomorphic augmentation e with its prescribed degree-zero component and every equivariant cochain map $L:P\to P[1]$ whose augmented degree-minus-one component sends $[g_0,g_1]$ to $a(g_0^{-1}g_1)$ on every profinite test object, the localized roof $\rho=Q(e[1]L)Q(e)^{-1}$, using the canonical single-complex and shift comparisons, equals $-\delta_a$, and $\Phi_1(\rho)=-[a]$, for the canonical shifted inflation adjunction of [lem-sfb-internal-inflation-graded-cup]. No finite-product assertion is made.

proof.text: On every profinite test object, $a(gh)=a(g)+a(h)$ makes the displayed action on $E_a$ associative, with identity and inverse actions, and natural in base change. The inclusion $i$ and projection $p$ are equivariant. Their underlying sequence is the split biproduct sequence, so it is exact in the action category by [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus]. By the free-module property in [lem-sfb-condensed-internal-bar-resolution], the natural generator formula $\ell[g]=(a(g),1)$ defines an internal $A$-linear map $P_0\to E_a$. It is equivariant because $\ell[hg]=(a(h)+a(g),1)=h\ell[g]$, and $p\ell=e$. Alternating deletion gives $\ell\partial_1[g_0,g_1]=(a(g_1)-a(g_0),0)=(a(g_0^{-1}g_1),0)$. Thus the unique map $f$ with $if=\ell\partial_1$ is specified by $f[g_0,g_1]=a(g_0^{-1}g_1)$. These are calculations on generalized generators, natural for every profinite base change, not claims that section modules are freely generated.

proof.text: Use the cone proof of the extension clause of lem-sfb-internal-bar-roof-adjunction directly in the prescribed coefficient localization. The kernel property of the extension inclusion i gives a unique f with f;i=partial_1;ell. Monicity of i and partial_1 partial_2=0 give partial_2;f=0. The generator formula in step 1 and freeness identify f with the assumed augmented component of L. Since A[1] is concentrated in degree -1, e[1]L is the single-component cocycle map fbar. The actual cone C(i) has A in degree -1, E_a in degree zero and differential i. Its map v:C(i)→A[0], given by the extension projection in degree zero, is a quasi-isomorphism by short exactness. The components f and ell define kappa:P→C(i); the prescribed degree-zero augmentation equation gives v kappa=e, while pr kappa=fbar. The canonical cone boundary is -Q(pr)Q(v)^(-1). Localize the two identities and cancel Q(e), obtaining Q(fbar)Q(e)^(-1)=-delta_a. Insert the canonical single-object localization and shift comparisons to obtain the displayed equality with singleδ. This uses the extension clause cone argument in the stated universe, rather than changing universes or selecting a Model.

proof.text: Write $R=R\Gamma_G$ and $\eta$ for the unit of the derived trivial-inflation adjunction. The unshifted adjoint of $\delta_a:A\to A[1]$ is $R(\delta_a)\circ\eta_A:A\to R(A[1])$. By [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-restriction-calculus], this is the adjunction normalized by the invariant inclusion and it uses the canonical shifts. Shift the last displayed arrow down by one using these comparisons. By the definition in [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class], it is exactly $[a]$: that definition applies derived invariants to the canonical extension boundary after the invariant unit $1$, then shifts down by one. Thus $\Phi_1(\delta_a)=[a]$. Additivity follows directly from the adjunction formula $R(u)\circ\eta_A$, since $R$ is additive and the shift identifications are additive. Therefore $\Phi_1(x_a)=-[a]$. In particular the sign here is forced by the cone boundary, not by choosing a different normalization of the character class.

theorem internalBarCharacterLiftNormalization
    (A : CondensedBar.Ring.{u}) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G]
    [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [T2Space G] [TotallyDisconnectedSpace G]
    (R : Resolution A.toMon G) (e : RoofAugmentation R) [QuasiIso e]
    (he : augmentationEquation R e) (a : Character A G)
    (L : complex R ⟶ (complex R)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧)
    (hL : ∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (x : Fin 2 → C(S, G)),
      onSections A.toMon
        ((termIso R 1).inv ≫ L.f (-1) ≫
          (CochainComplex.shiftFunctorObjXIso (complex R) 1 (-1) 0 rfl).hom ≫
            (termIso R 0).hom ≫ R.augmentation).val S
        (basis A.toMon G 2 (R.objects 1) (R.freeIso 1) S x) =
          a.app S ((x 0)⁻¹ * x 1)) :
    let rho : coefficient A G ⟶ (coefficient A G)⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ :=
      localizedShiftedRoof DerivedCategory.Q.{u + 1} e
        ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ (Equivariant A G) 0).app
          (regularTrivial A G)) (1 : ℤ) L
    rho = -(extensionExact a).singleδ ∧
      inflationPhi A G 1 rho = -characterClass a
